title: Detection of Plasmodium Infection by Nested Polymerase Chain Reaction Assay
author: Unknown

materials: 3.2 Preparation and storage of reagents 3.2.1 Stock reagents for PCR (e.g. Primers at 100mM, dNTP nucleotides for dNTPs) and enzymes should be stored at -20°C. Stock reagents should be diluted into working concentrations and aliquoted into separate tubes. Working dilutions of PCR reagents (10X buffer, dNTPs, MgCl2, primers at 10µM) should be stored in the -20°C freezer for long term storage (i.e. over one week) but can be stored in the fridge if in frequent use and retrieved for use when required. Working aliquots of sample and control DNA as well as primary PCR (Nest-1) products must be kept at -20°C for long term storage but if in daily use can be kept in the fridge. Working aliquots of PCR reagents must be discarded after opening several times (e.g. over 10 times).
5. Equipment and Materia ls Trough Pipette 10µl presterilized filter tips 20µl presterilized filter tips 200µl presterilized filter tips 1000µl presterilized filter tips 96 well plate Plate seal
6. Reagents and Chemicals Nuclease free H2O Buffer (thermopol) dNTPs Taq polymerase DNA Forward and reverse primers

steps.title: Decontaminate work area and equipment
steps.instruction: Clean benches, work stations, centrifuges, vortexes and pipettes with 10 % bleach followed by 70 % ethanol before and after every PCR set‑up; change gloves regularly, especially before dispensing master mixes; use aerosol‑resistant filtered tips and dedicated blue‑tagged pre‑PCR pipettes; wear gloves at all times.

steps.title: Store and aliquot extracted DNA
steps.instruction: After DNA extraction (robotic or manual) store the eluted DNA at –20 °C; transfer a 20 µl aliquot of each sample into a well of a sterile 96‑well plate or an Eppendorf tube for diagnostic PCR and speciation; keep the remaining stock for long‑term storage and do not use it until after PCR is set up.

steps.title: Plan plate layout and include controls
steps.instruction: For each 96‑well plate include eight controls (four positive, four negative) randomised among the 80 sample wells; add additional 3D7 extracted‑DNA controls at the PCR stage; for bar‑coded samples print the plate plan and record in the lab book the date, experiment, target gene, Nest‑1 or Nest‑2, master‑mix recipe, thermal cycler number and block; for non‑bar‑coded samples prepare the same information manually.

steps.title: Prepare PCR master mix
steps.instruction: In a clean DNA‑free area (preferably a sterile laminar‑flow hood) using only blue‑tagged pre‑PCR pipettes, disinfect the pipettes and bench/hood with 10 % bleach then 70 % ethanol; thaw, vortex and spin down all reagents except Taq polymerase (keep Taq frozen until all other reagents are added); add master‑mix components in the order listed in the SOP tables into a clean trough, mix gently with a P1000 tip by pipetting up‑and‑down several times while tilting the trough to avoid foaming; label the sterile PCR plate with study initials, plate number, primer name, “PCR”, date and operator initials.

steps.title: Calculate and dispense master mix volume
steps.instruction: Calculate master‑mix volume for the number of reactions plus 10 extra to cover pipetting loss and dead volume; e.g., for a full plate of 88 reactions (80 samples + 8 controls) prepare mix for 105 reactions; dispense 11 µl of master mix into each well designated for primary/Nest‑1 reactions and 14 µl into each well designated for Nest‑2 reactions; dispense 15 µl into wells A12, B12 and C12 as PCR negative controls.

steps.title: Add template DNA or Nest‑1 product
steps.instruction: Briefly spin down the DNA extracts or Nest‑1 PCR products at maximum speed; add 4 µl of extracted DNA to each primary/Nest‑1 well or 1 µl of Nest‑1 product to each Nest‑2 well according to the plate plan; seal the plate, spin down again, and place it in the thermal cycler to start the appropriate PCR run.

steps.title: Run PCR with specified cycling conditions
steps.instruction:
Perform two sequential PCRs:
• Nest‑1 (outer) with primers rPLU5 + rPLU6: 94 °C 3 min; 94 °C 30 s; 58 °C 30 s; 24 cycles; 72 °C 45 s; final 72 °C 5 min.
• Nest‑2 (inner) either with generic Plasmo1 + Plasmo2 primers (94 °C 3 min; 94 °C 30 s; 58 °C 30 s; 29 cycles; 72 °C 45 s; final 72 °C 5 min) or with species‑specific primer pairs (rFAL1 + rFAL2, rMAL1 + rMAL2, rOVA1 + rOVA2, rVIV1 + rVIV2) using 94 °C 3 min; 94 °C 30 s; 60 °C 30 s; 29 cycles; 72 °C 45 s; final 72 °C 5 min. Both reactions are 15 µl total volume.

steps.title: Post‑PCR handling and analysis
steps.instruction: After each PCR run, briefly spin the plate, then store it at 4 °C or –20 °C for later use (Nest‑1 plates can be stored for subsequent Nest‑2 reactions); alternatively, proceed directly to QIAxcel analysis of Nest‑2 products as described in SOP_MDX_QIAxcel; export sample IDs from the Item Tracker, convert to XML with the dedicated software, and upload the XML file to QIAxcel to avoid manual transcription.

steps.title: Calculate concentrations and report results
steps.instruction: Use the dilution equation C1·V1 = C2·V2 (or V1 = C2·V2/C1) to compute any required concentrations or volumes, ensuring consistent units (e.g., mM for concentration, µl for volume); generate an Excel scoring sheet, have two independent readers score the PCR results, and resolve any discrepancies with a third (supervisor) reader.

description: 7.2 Summary of PCR 7.2.1 Primary PCR/ Nest-1 PCR should be done using rPLU5 + rPLU6 primers. 7.2.2 For each plate include a negative control of PCR mix without a DNA template. 7.2.3 If required, include positive controls for falciparum, ovale, vivax and malariae species. 7.2.4 Nest-2 PCR to determine the presence of Plasmodium infection should be done using the genus-specific primers Plasmo1 + Plasmo 2. 7.2.5 Presence of Plasmodium falciparum species is determined by running a Nest-2 PCR for all plasmodium positive samples using species-specific primers rFAL 1 + rFAL 2. 7.2.6 If required to determine presence of other species from Plasmodium falciparum negative samples, run Nest-2 PCR assays using other species-specific primers 7.2.7 For the determination of the different Plasmodium species present in samples, use the species-specific primers indicated below in the PCR mastermix (mixes prepared separately): Plasmodium falciparum use rFAL 1 + rFAL 2 Plasmodium ovale use rOVA 1 + rOVA 2 Plasmodium vivax use rVIV 1 + rVIV 2 Plasmodium malariae use rMAL 1 + rMAL 2 7.2.8 Note the PCR programme name and thermal cycler machine number (e.g. #B..........) and block number (in the case of the tetrad) used for the PCR reaction in your lab book. 7.2.9 Once the PCR run is complete, remove plate and briefly centrifuge to spin down products. 7.2.10 Store PCR plates in the fridge or freezer 7.2.11 Run the plate on the QIAxcel advanced system to determine if the PCR has worked and PCR fragment size. Alternatively samples can be run on Agarose gel electrophoresis using Ethidium Bromide. 7.2.12 Score results as presence or absence of bands comparing with control bands. Scoring should be done either by two independent readers, or by one reader and automated binary scoring using the QIAxcel screen gel software. Discrepancies are settled with a third read (ideally by the supervisor). Unresolved discrepancies should be repeated.
